pick.wrong: Have another look, then try again.

dry-plant.ask: The leaves are dry and drooping. What does this plant need?
dry-plant.clue: Think about what you give a plant every day.
dry-plant.why: Plants need water. The roots drink it up from the soil.

no.dark: Plants need light, not darkness, to grow.

plant-food.ask: What do plants need to make their own food?
plant-food.clue: Green leaves turn toward the sky. What are they catching?
plant-food.why: Green leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant.

no.rice: Plants do not eat food like we do. They make their own.
no.milk: Plants do not drink milk. They make their own food.

fish-air.ask: A fish lives in water. Does a fish need air?
fish-air.why: Yes. A fish breathes with its gills. Gills take in the air that is mixed into the water.

c.yes: Yes, it gets air from the water

no.no: All animals need air. A fish gets its air from the water.

no-food.ask: Which one does NOT need food?
no-food.why: A toy robot is not alive. Living things need food. Toys do not.

no.cat: A cat is alive, so it needs food.
no.hen: A hen is alive, so it needs food.
no.child: You are alive, so you need food!

rice-water.ask: Why do farmers keep water in rice fields?
rice-water.clue: Rice is a plant. What do plants need?
rice-water.why: Rice plants need lots of water to grow. They grow well in wet fields.

c.grow: Rice plants need water to grow

no.white: Water does not change the colour of rice. The plants need it to grow.

puppy.ask: What does a puppy need to grow?
puppy.clue: What do you need every day to grow?
puppy.why: Animals need food, water and air to live and grow.

no.sun: Plants make food from sunlight. Animals must eat food.

hear.ask: The rooster crows. Which part helps you hear it?
hear.clue: Sounds go into the sides of your head.
hear.why: We hear sounds with our ears.

smell.ask: You smell a durian. Which part helps you smell?
smell.clue: Which part do you hold when something smells bad?

taste.ask: A green mango tastes sour. Which part tastes it?
taste.why: We taste with our tongue: sweet, sour, salty and bitter.

see.ask: You see a rainbow. Which part helps you see?
see.clue: You close them when you sleep.

feel.ask: Ice feels cold. Which part feels it?
feel.clue: What do you touch things with?
feel.why: Our skin feels hot and cold, soft and rough.

sun-safe.ask: Is it safe to look straight at the Sun?
sun-safe.clue: Your eyes are precious. How do you keep them safe?
sun-safe.why: No. The Sun is so bright it can hurt your eyes. Never look straight at it.

c.no: No, it can hurt your eyes

no.yes: Looking at the Sun can hurt your eyes, even for a short time.

smoke.ask: You smell smoke at home. What should you do?
smoke.clue: Smoke can mean fire. Who can help?
smoke.why: Tell a grown-up at once. Your nose can warn you of danger.

no.sleep: Smoke can mean a fire. Always tell a grown-up straight away.

water.ask: Which part takes in water from the soil?
water.why: Roots grow down into the soil and soak up water.

no.leaf: Leaves are up in the light. The water is in the soil.

hold.ask: Which part holds the plant up straight?
hold.clue: It is long, like a pole, between the roots and the leaves.
hold.why: The stem holds the plant up and carries water to the leaves.

food.ask: Which part uses sunlight to make food?
food.clue: It is green and flat, and faces the Sun.
food.why: Green leaves use sunlight, air and water to make food for the plant.

no.root: Roots are in the dark soil. Making food needs sunlight.

fruit.ask: Which part can grow into a fruit?
fruit.clue: Mango trees have these before they have mangoes.
fruit.why: A flower can grow into a fruit with seeds inside.

new-tree.ask: Which part of a mango can grow into a new mango tree?
new-tree.clue: It is big and hard, in the middle of the fruit.
new-tree.why: The seed can grow into a new plant.

lotus.ask: A lotus grows in a pond. Which part is down in the mud?
lotus.why: Lotus roots grow in the mud. The leaves and flower reach up to the light.

fish.clue: Watch a fish move. What swishes from side to side?
fish.why: A fish swims by moving its fins and tail.

no.gills: Gills help a fish breathe, not swim.
no.scales: Scales cover the fish and keep it safe.

bird.clue: A bird flaps them up and down.
bird.why: Birds flap their wings to fly.

no.beak: A beak helps a bird eat. It does not help it fly.

turtle.ask: What keeps a turtle safe from danger?
turtle.clue: A turtle can hide inside it.
turtle.why: A turtle pulls its head and legs into its hard shell.

duck.ask: Why can a duck swim so well?
duck.why: Skin between a duck's toes pushes the water, like a paddle.

elephant.ask: What does an elephant use to pick up food and drink water?
elephant.clue: It is very long, at the front of its face.
elephant.why: An elephant's trunk is its long nose. It grabs food and sucks up water.

rabbit.ask: Why does a rabbit have big ears?
rabbit.why: Big ears catch quiet sounds, so a rabbit can hear danger and run away.

tadpole.ask: This baby is a tadpole. What does it grow into?
tadpole.clue: It lives in a pond and grows legs.
tadpole.why: A tadpole grows legs, loses its tail and becomes a frog.

no.fish: A tadpole swims like a fish, but it grows legs and becomes a frog.

chick.ask: This baby is a chick. What does it grow into?
chick.clue: It hatches from a hen's egg.
chick.why: A chick grows into a hen or a rooster, like its parents.

no.duck: A baby duck is a duckling. A chick grows into a hen or a rooster.

caterpillar.ask: This baby is a caterpillar. What does it grow into?
caterpillar.clue: It has bright wings when it is grown.
caterpillar.why: A caterpillar makes a case called a chrysalis, then comes out as a butterfly.

kittens.ask: Kittens and their mother. How do they look?
kittens.clue: Look at the colours and spots.
kittens.why: Babies look like their parents, but not exactly the same.

c.alike: Alike, but not exactly the same

no.same: Look again. The kittens have different spots and colours.

mango-seed.ask: A mango seed is planted. What does it grow into?
mango-seed.clue: A seed grows into the same kind of plant it came from.
mango-seed.why: A mango seed grows into a mango tree.

puppies.ask: Puppies from one family. Can they be different colours?
puppies.why: Yes. Puppies look like their parents, but they can have different colours and spots.

no.never: Look at the puppies. Brothers and sisters can be different colours.

hen-eggs.ask: Why does a hen sit on her eggs?
hen-eggs.why: Eggs need to stay warm so the chicks inside can grow.

bird-feed.ask: Baby birds open their beaks and call. What does the parent do?
bird-feed.clue: Baby birds cannot fly to find food yet.
bird-feed.why: The parent brings them food until they can find their own.

cat-carry.ask: Why does a mother cat carry her kitten in her mouth?
cat-carry.clue: Kittens are too small to walk far.
cat-carry.why: She moves it to a safe place. She holds the loose skin on its neck gently.

baby-cry.ask: A baby cries. What do the parents do?
baby-cry.why: Crying is how a baby says it is hungry, tired or hurting. Parents find out what it needs.

c.needs: Find out what the baby needs

no.leave: A baby cannot look after itself. Crying is how it asks for help.

ducklings.ask: Why do ducklings follow their mother?
ducklings.clue: Where is it safest for a little duckling?
ducklings.why: Staying close keeps them safe, and they learn how to find food.

crocodile.ask: A mother crocodile stays near her nest. Why?
crocodile.clue: Other animals like to eat eggs.
crocodile.why: She guards her eggs so other animals cannot eat them.

hum.ask: Put your hand on your throat and hum. What do you feel?
hum.why: A buzzing shake. Sound is made when something shakes fast. We call it a vibration.

drum.ask: You hit a drum. What does the top of the drum do?
drum.clue: Sound comes from things that shake.
drum.why: The drum top shakes fast. The shaking makes the sound.

no.still: If it stayed still, there would be no sound. Sound comes from shaking.

bell.ask: A bell is ringing. You hold it tight. What happens?
bell.clue: Your hand stops the bell from shaking.
bell.why: The sound stops, because the bell cannot shake any more.

no.same: Holding the bell stops it shaking. No shaking, no sound.

rice.ask: Put rice grains on a drum, then hit the drum. What do the grains do?
rice.clue: The drum top shakes when you hit it.
rice.why: They jump! The shaking drum makes the rice move.

harder.ask: You hit the drum harder. How does it sound?
harder.clue: A harder hit makes a bigger shake.
harder.why: Louder. A bigger shake makes a louder sound.

no.quieter: A harder hit makes the drum shake more, so it is louder.

string.ask: You pluck a guitar string. When does the sound stop?
string.clue: Watch the string after you pluck it.
string.why: The sound stops when the string stops shaking.

no.never: The string slowly stops shaking, and then the sound stops.

cave.ask: Deep in a cave with no light at all. Can you see your hand?
cave.clue: What do you need to see in a dark room?
cave.why: No. We can only see things when there is light.

c.no: No, we need light to see

no.yes: With no light at all, no one can see, even by looking hard.

moon.ask: Why does the Moon shine at night?
moon.clue: The Moon is a big ball of rock.
moon.why: The Sun shines on the Moon. The Moon does not make its own light.

no.own: The Moon is rock. It makes no light. It shines because the Sun lights it up.
no.lamp: The Moon is a ball of rock, not a lamp. The Sun lights it up.

shadow.clue: Stand in the sun. Where does your shadow go?
shadow.why: Something blocks the light, so a dark shape forms behind it.

no.water: A shadow is not wet. It is where light cannot reach.

mirror.ask: You shine a torch at a mirror. What does the light do?
mirror.clue: When you look in a mirror, you see yourself.
mirror.why: It bounces back. Mirrors are smooth and shiny, so light bounces off them.

no.through: Light cannot pass through a mirror. It bounces off.

dark-room.ask: Your room is dark. How can you see your toys?
dark-room.clue: What do we need to see?
dark-room.why: Turn on a light. We need light to see.

cat-dark.ask: Can a cat see when there is no light at all?
cat-dark.clue: Do any eyes work with no light?
cat-dark.why: No. Cats see well in dim light, but with no light at all, no one can see.

c.no: No, cats need some light too

no.yes: Cats see well in dim light. But every eye needs some light to see.

rise.ask: Where does the Sun rise in the morning?
rise.clue: It rises on the same side every morning.
rise.why: The Sun rises in the east every morning.

set.ask: Where does the Sun set in the evening?
set.clue: It sets on the other side from where it rose.
set.why: The Sun sets in the west every evening.

high.ask: When is the Sun highest in the sky?
high.clue: It climbs in the morning and goes down in the afternoon.
high.why: Around midday, the Sun is at its highest.

stars.ask: Why can't we see stars in the daytime?
stars.clue: Can you see a torch in bright sunshine?
stars.why: The stars are still there. The bright Sun hides them.

no.away: The stars are always there. The Sun's light is so bright we cannot see them.
no.sleep: Stars do not sleep. The Sun's light is so bright we cannot see them.

day-moon.ask: Can you sometimes see the Moon in the daytime?
day-moon.clue: Look up on a clear afternoon.
day-moon.why: Yes. The Moon is often in the sky during the day too.

no.no: Look up on a clear day. You can often see a pale Moon.

short-shadow.clue: Shadows are short when the Sun is high.
short-shadow.why: Around midday. When the Sun is high, shadows are short. When it is low, they are long.

moon-shape.ask: Does the Moon look the same shape every night?
moon-shape.clue: Look at the Moon for a few nights.
moon-shape.why: No. Its shape seems to change each night, and the pattern repeats about every month.

no.round: Watch for a few nights. The Moon goes from thin to round and back again.

rainy.ask: In Cambodia, when is the rainy season?
rainy.clue: It starts around the middle of the year.
rainy.why: Cambodia's rainy season is about May to October. The dry season is about November to April.

dry.ask: Which month is in Cambodia's dry season?
dry.clue: The dry season is about November to April.
dry.why: January is in the dry season. There is little rain.

rice.ask: When do Cambodian farmers plant most of their rice?
rice.why: When the rains come. Rice needs lots of water to grow.

c.dry: When the fields are dry and dusty

no.dry: Rice needs lots of water, so most rice is planted when the rains come.

storm.ask: Dark clouds and thunder are coming. Where should you go?
storm.why: Go inside a building. That is the safest place in a storm.

no.tree: Lightning often hits tall trees. Go inside a building.
no.river: Water is dangerous in a storm. Go inside a building.

long-day.ask: In Cambodia, which month has longer days?
long-day.clue: The middle of the year has a little more daylight.
long-day.why: June. In Cambodia, June days are more than an hour longer than December days.

cool.ask: What helps you stay cool on a hot, dry day?
cool.clue: The Sun warms everything it shines on.
cool.why: Shade blocks the Sun, and drinking water cools your body.

living.ask: Is it living or not living?
living.rule: Living things eat or drink, grow, and have babies.

why.dog: A dog eats, grows and has puppies. It is living.
why.car: A car moves, but it does not eat, grow or have babies.
why.tree: A tree drinks water, grows and makes seeds. It is living.
why.ball: A ball can roll, but it does not grow or eat.
why.fish: A fish eats, grows and lays eggs. It is living.
why.robot: A toy robot moves, but it is not alive. It does not eat or grow.
why.flower: A flower drinks water, grows and makes seeds. It is living.
why.rock: A rock does not eat, drink or grow.
why.snail: A snail eats leaves, grows and lays eggs. It is living.
why.book: A book does not eat, drink or grow.
why.rice: A rice plant drinks water, grows and makes new rice grains. It is living.
why.cup: A cup does not eat, drink or grow.

lightsource.ask: Does it make its own light?
lightsource.rule: Some things make light. Others only shine when light falls on them.

why.sun: The Sun makes its own light. It lights up the whole day.
why.moon: The Moon makes no light. It shines because the Sun lights it up.
why.lamp: A lamp makes light when it is switched on.
why.mirror: A mirror bounces light, but it makes none.
why.spoon: A shiny spoon bounces light. It does not make it.
why.torch: A torch makes light when you switch it on.
why.book: A book makes no light. We see it when light shines on it.
why.firefly: A firefly makes its own light, to talk to other fireflies.
why.rock: A rock makes no light. We see it when light shines on it.

lightpath.rule: Clear things let light through. Some things let a little through. Others block it.

why.window: Light goes straight through clear glass. You can see through it.
why.paper: Thin paper lets some light through, but you cannot see clearly through it.
why.door: A wooden door blocks the light.
why.glass: Clear water and glass let light through.
why.cloth: Thin cloth lets some light through, but not all.
why.pot: A metal pot blocks the light.
why.bottle: A clear bottle lets light through.
why.bag: A cloudy bag lets some light through, but you cannot see clearly.
why.wall: A brick wall blocks all the light.

order.wrong: Something is out of order. Tap a card to take it back.

mango.ask: How does a mango tree grow? Put it in order.
mango.clue: Every plant starts as a seed.
mango.why: A seed grows a sprout, then a young tree, then a big tree with fruit.

chicken.ask: How does a chicken grow? Put it in order.
chicken.why: An egg hatches into a chick, and the chick grows into a hen.

frog.ask: How does a frog grow? Put it in order.
frog.clue: Frogs lay their eggs in water.
frog.why: Eggs hatch into tadpoles. Tadpoles grow legs and become froglets, then frogs.

butterfly.ask: How does a butterfly grow? Put it in order.
butterfly.clue: The caterpillar comes before the wings.
butterfly.why: An egg hatches into a caterpillar. It makes a chrysalis, and a butterfly comes out.

person.ask: How does a person grow? Put it in order.
person.why: A baby grows into a child, and a child grows into a grown-up.

rice.ask: How does rice grow? Put it in order.
rice.clue: Rice is green while it grows, and turns golden when it is ready.
rice.why: Young rice plants grow tall and green, turn golden, then farmers harvest the grain.

sun.ask: Put the Sun's day in order.
sun.clue: The day starts when the Sun comes up.
sun.why: The Sun rises, climbs high at midday, sets in the evening, and then it is night.

moon.ask: The Moon grows night by night. Put it in order.
moon.clue: It starts as a thin curve.
moon.why: A thin crescent grows to a half Moon, then a full Moon.

shadow.ask: Put the tree's shadow in order, from morning to evening.
shadow.clue: In the morning the Sun is low in the east.
shadow.why: Morning shadows are long. At midday they are short. In the evening they are long again, on the other side.
